lines.japanese: だからってわけじゃないけど、このまままっすぐ高速道路の下へ向かうのはなんていうか……なんていうかだった。
lines.english: That wasn't the reason, exactly. Even so, heading straight back beneath the expressway felt... I didn't know. It felt like something.

lines.japanese: つまり、どこか暇人たちの集まる場所で暇潰しをしたい気分。
lines.english: What I wanted was to kill time wherever people with time to kill gathered.

lines.japanese: たとえばパルクレープ。
lines.english: Paru Crêpes, for instance.

lines.japanese: しかしパルさんは金土の夜でもないかぎり、だいたい１１時には店を畳みはじめる。いまから向かっても無駄足の可能性が高い。
lines.english: But unless it was Friday or Saturday, Paru usually started packing up around eleven. If I went now, chances were I'd make the trip for nothing.

lines.japanese: 分かってはいるのに、それでもいつになく往生際の悪い俺は、なんとなくピンフ通りのあの場所へ歩きだしていた。
lines.english: I knew that. Yet I was unusually unwilling to admit defeat, and somehow my feet carried me toward that spot on Pinfu Street anyway.

lines.japanese: 道中、どこか遠くからジェンベの音が聴こえてきた。孤独なカラスは夜に鳴く。
lines.english: Along the way, a djembe sounded somewhere far off. A lonely crow cries at night.

lines.japanese: 予想通り、ピンクのミニバンはどこにも見当たらなかった。
lines.english: As expected, the pink minivan was nowhere in sight.

lines.japanese: パルさんは撤収するとき、停車していた場所とその付近にいつもホーキをかけていくから、パルクレープ跡地は嫌味かと思うぐらい綺麗なもんだった。
lines.english: Whenever Paru packed up, she swept her parking spot and the ground around it. The patch where Paru Crêpes had stood was so spotless it felt almost like a reproach.

lines.japanese: もしかしたらメンマの店に寄ってるかも……いや、それはねえか、もう遅いし。パルさんはその辺しっかりしてるから、こんな時間からあいつを連れまわしたりはしないだろう。
lines.english: Maybe she'd stopped by Menma's... No, not this late. Paru was responsible about that sort of thing. She wouldn't drag the kid around at this hour.
Hm...

lines.japanese: そこで俺は気付いた。いつの間にかクレープ屋やラーメン屋へ暇つぶしに行くことより、あのいじくって遊ぶと面白い小娘に遭遇することが第一義となっている。
lines.english: And then I realized. Somewhere along the way, killing time at the crêpe or ramen stand had become secondary. My real priority had become running into that little girl who was so much fun to tease.

lines.japanese: なんだそりゃ。お笑い種じゃないか。
lines.english: What the hell was that? I was a joke.

lines.japanese: 俺は個室ビデオ屋の壁に背中を預けた。このもどかしくて珍妙な感情について、しばし考察しようとした。
lines.english: I leaned against the wall of a private video-booth shop and tried to examine this strange, frustrating feeling for a while.

lines.japanese: しかし目を閉じた途端、その雑居ビルの細い階段からわいのわいのと騒がしい集団が下りてきて、おまけにそこから動かずわいのわいのと騒がしく語らいはじめた。
lines.english: The instant I closed my eyes, however, a rowdy crowd spilled down the mixed-use building's narrow stairs. Worse, they planted themselves there and kept right on making a racket.

lines.japanese: 三人、四人、五人……どんどん増えて、ゲーム屋から出てきた小学生みたいにはしゃいでる。うざい。超うざい。思考の妨げもいいところだ。
lines.english: Three, four, five... They kept multiplying, carrying on like grade-school kids just out of a game shop. Annoying. So goddamn annoying. I could hardly hear myself think.

lines.japanese: 「ぶはー！　もうマジしょっぱいわ～。やっぱねぇ、ゴメとデイトリが規制された時点で脱法系は終わってたンよ。その後もまあ、メチとかエースあたりはまだ使えたけど、今もう、そんなんすらアウトでしょう」
lines.english: “Phew! The scene is seriously pathetic now. Once Five-MeO and Daytripper got scheduled, that was it for legal highs. Methylone and Ace still worked for a while, but now even those are out, right?”

lines.japanese: しかも聞いてて趣のある話ならともかく、さっぱり意味不明の単語が頻出するから理解さえ出来ない。ＴＶゲームのアイテム談義か何かだろうか。いい歳して元気な男の子たちだ。
lines.english: It might have been different if the conversation were at least interesting, but incomprehensible words kept cropping up and I couldn't make head or tail of it. Were they discussing video-game items or something? Remarkably energetic boys for their age.

lines.japanese: ＴＶゲームなんて俺には、脱衣麻雀と、メダルを賭ける競馬ゲームと、ウイングクエストのいっちゃん古いやつぐらいしか馴染みがない。そもそも今はあまり「ＴＶゲーム」なんて言い方しないんだろうか。
lines.english: As far as “TV games” went, about all I knew were strip mahjong, medal-betting horse-racing machines, and the very first *Wing Quest*. Did anyone even call them “TV games” anymore?

lines.japanese: 「ちゅーかもう合法でも違法でも、どのみちケミは終焉迎えてるンよねー。いま出回ってるバツなんて、多幸ナシでただアガるだけのシャブ玉ばっかよ。エルは供給自体が減ってるしさ、もうサイケ流行らんのよね」
lines.english: “Legal or illegal, chems are dead either way. All the E going around now is speed in a pill—gets you high without making you happy. Supply of L is drying up too. Psychedelics just aren't in anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「Ａｗ、ウェイトウェイト、落ちつけよオメエ。語りすぎで流石に引くわ。ロスの路地裏じゃねえんだからよ、ちったあ自重してくれよ」
lines.english: “Whoa, wait, wait. Settle down, man. That's way too much information. This isn't some back alley in L.A. Show a little restraint.”

lines.japanese: 「ねーねー、そんじゃさあ、アレってどーなんスか。あのほら、新型のアシッドとかいう？　最近日本でも流通始まったっつう噂もあんじゃないスか。名前なんつったっけ……エロイデス？　や、グロイデスか」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, what about that one? You know, the new acid or whatever? They say it’s started circulating in Japan lately too. What was it called... Lustorious? No, Gore-ious?”

lines.japanese: 「あ～、例の？　グロリアスでしょ、アレはねぇ～……」
lines.english: “Oh, that one? Glorious, right? See, the thing about that...”

lines.japanese: グロリアス？　なんだ、聞き覚えのある単語だな。
lines.english: Glorious? That rang a bell.

lines.japanese: ん？　つうか？　それ以前にこいつらの声、つうか喋り方、どっかで聞き覚えがあるような……？
lines.english: Hm? More to the point—hadn't I heard these voices, or at least these ways of talking, somewhere before...?
“Ugh.”

lines.japanese: しかし俺は目を開けて後悔した。
lines.english: I opened my eyes and immediately regretted it.
“Oh?”

lines.japanese: 「おおっ？」
lines.english: “Ooh?”

lines.japanese: 「おおおー！」
lines.english: “Oooooh!”

lines.japanese: こいつら……だったのかよ……。
lines.english: These idiots. Of course it was them...

lines.japanese: 俺はビデオ屋の壁にもたれたまま、うなだれる気力もなく濁った瞳で答えた。
lines.english: Still leaning against the video-shop wall, too drained even to hang my head, I answered with dead eyes.

lines.japanese: そして追い討ちをかけるように、同じ階段から下りてきたもう二人。
lines.english: Then, as if to finish me off, two more people came down the same staircase.

lines.japanese: 「おー」
lines.english: “Yo.”

lines.japanese: ……こいつら……までかよ……。
lines.english: ...These two too...

lines.japanese: 「やっひー！　隼人君じゃあーん！」
lines.english: “Heyyy! It's Hayato!”

lines.japanese: 「ぐぼっ！」
lines.english: “Guh!”

lines.japanese: 例によって香田が飛びついてきた。俺はビデオ屋の壁と、やつの香水臭い体とに挟まれ──
lines.english: As usual, Koda threw herself at me. I was crushed between the video-shop wall and her perfume-drenched body—

lines.japanese: ──ん、あれ、べつに香ってねえな。なんだこいつ、今日はいつものアレ切らしてんのか。まあ、どうでもいい話。
lines.english: —Hm? Wait. She didn't smell of anything. What, had she run out of her usual stuff today? Not that it mattered.

lines.japanese: 「亜衣、よせってホラ。成田いやがってっから」
lines.english: “Ai, come on, get off him. Narita hates that.”

lines.japanese: 「えー」
lines.english: “Aww.”

lines.japanese: 幼馴染みに引っぺがされて香田の体が離れていった。自由を得た俺は溜息と共にこうべを垂れる。
lines.english: Her childhood friend peeled her off me. My freedom restored, I let my head fall with a sigh.

lines.japanese: 「はああ……なんで俺ンとこにはこう、いつもいつも、探してもねーやつに限って現れんだよ……」
lines.english: “Haaaaah... Why is it always the people I'm not looking for who turn up...?”

lines.japanese: 「エエ？　なんスか隼人先輩、そんな他人行儀にアタマ下げないでよ」
lines.english: “Huh? What's with the bow, Hayato? We're not strangers.”

lines.japanese: 「おじぎじゃねーよ。うんざりのボディランゲージだよ」
lines.english: “I'm not bowing. That's my body saying it's sick of this shit.”

lines.japanese: 「つか、なに、おまえらどこ行ってたの」
lines.english: “Anyway, where did you people just come from?”

lines.japanese: 俺はやつらが連れだって下りてきた、節操ない色合いの怪しいビルを見上げた。建物脇に張りだした細長い看板には、おげれつな創意工夫を凝らした店名や、意味不明な横文字の店名が縦一列に並んでいた。
lines.english: I looked up at the suspicious building they had descended from, painted in a riot of colors with no sense of restraint whatsoever. A long, narrow signboard projected from its side, listing one tastelessly inventive shop name after another, interspersed with meaningless foreign names.

lines.japanese: 「四階の店だよ～」
lines.english: “The place on the fourth floor.”
“The fourth floor...?”

lines.japanese: 外壁の窓を下から四つ数えた。ビビッドな色合いの単細胞生物を散りばめたようなグラフィックボードが、店内を隠すように窓ガラスを覆っていた。店の名前は妖しくひん曲がった欧文で、解読する気にもならない。
lines.english: I counted four windows up from the ground. A graphic panel covered in what looked like single-celled organisms in vivid colors concealed the glass. The shop’s name writhed across it in sinister Western lettering I had no desire to decipher.

lines.japanese: 「まァ、若い衆のためにな、Ｈｕｈ、ちょっとした社会勉強さ」
lines.english: “Well, we thought we'd give the youngsters a little education. Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　なにアレ四階。アレ何屋さんなの」
lines.english: “What is that fourth-floor place, anyway? What kind of store is it?”

lines.japanese: 「何屋？　ああ、そいや何屋っつうんスかアレ？　輸入雑貨屋？」
lines.english: “What kind? Huh. What *would* you call it? An import shop?”

lines.japanese: 「うんとねー、民族衣装とか外国のパイプとか植物の種とか、あとレゲエのＣＤとか売ってた系ー」
lines.english: “Um, they had traditional clothes, foreign pipes, plant seeds, reggae CDs—stuff like that.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ヘッドショップな……」
lines.english: “Ah. A head shop...”

lines.japanese: パイプやボングなんかの喫煙具、あるいはハーブやお香といったリラクゼーショングッズを並べている店。もちろん法律や条令に触れるものは置いてない。ただし、どういった用途に用いるかは買っていった客次第だ。
lines.english: A shop selling smoking gear—pipes and bongs—and nominal relaxation goods such as herbs and incense. Naturally, nothing on its shelves violated any law or ordinance. What a customer did with it afterward was another matter.

lines.japanese: 「コーダイン、ご感想は～？」
lines.english: “So, Kodine—verdict?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、あんま面白くなかった。なーんかお香くさいし、変なユラユラした曲流れてるし、やなカンジー」
lines.english: “It wasn't that interesting. It stank like incense, and they had this weird, wobbly music playing. I didn't like it.”

lines.japanese: 「グッド。いつまでもそのピュアなハートを忘れちゃいけねえぜ、日本のお嬢ちゃん」
lines.english: “Good. Never lose that pure heart, fair maiden of Japan.”

lines.japanese: 「さて、次の社会勉強はどこに行くか……」
lines.english: “Now then, where shall we go for our next educational field trip...?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ＬＲさん！　つつつ次ッ、次は俺、女体の神秘を学べるとこ社会見学したいッス！」
lines.english: “Wait, LR! N-n-next I wanna tour someplace where I can study the mysteries of the female body!”

lines.japanese: 「だめー！　邪念のある子はだめー！」
lines.english: “No! No wicked children allowed!”

lines.japanese: 「ンー、じゃあ、どーすっかあ。ヤーさんの事務所が入ってそうなビルで、ロシアン・ピンポンダッシュでもすっかあ」
lines.english: “Hmm. What, then? Find a building that looks like it has a yakuza office and play Russian ding-dong ditch?”

lines.japanese: 「あーあー、ガキ連れてしょーもねえ暇潰ししてんなあ、おまえら」
lines.english: “Look at you, dragging kids around town to waste time on this pathetic crap.”

lines.japanese: 俺は悪趣味な引率者たちに、あからさまな呆れと軽蔑の目を向けてやった。
lines.english: I gave their tasteless chaperones an undisguised look of contempt.

lines.japanese: 「ア～イ、まあ、ごもっともなんだけどお」
lines.english: “Aye, well, you've got us there.”

lines.japanese: レゲエ風があくびの出そうな顔でうなずく。ハゲやギャル男がしみじみ同意の表情を見せた。
lines.english: The guy in reggae gear nodded, looking bored enough to yawn. The bald guy and the flashy kid looked equally convinced.

lines.japanese: 「でもよお、実際ヒマなんだよなァ、太平の世の武士っつうのは」
lines.english: “But we really are bored. We're samurai in an age of peace.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぁ～あ……どっかにこう、Ｒ－ウィングに代わる、次世代の悪モンでもいないもんスかねえ」
lines.english: “Yaaawn... Think there's some next-generation villain out there to take R-Wing's place?”

lines.japanese: 「大体さー、あの子ら降参すんの早過ぎなんよ。そんな簡単にあだ討ち諦めちゃっちゃー、愛しのハリューちゃんも浮かばれないよネ～」
lines.english: “That bunch surrendered way too fast. Give up on vengeance that easily and their beloved Haryu will never rest in peace.”

lines.japanese: やつらの会話に、今度は俺の知ってる単語が出てきた。Ｒ－ウィング。そしてハリュー・クロード。ガード下の派手な茶番劇が思いだされる。今日はあの未明の事件から二度目の夜だった。
lines.english: This time, their conversation produced words I knew. R-Wing. Haryu Claude. The gaudy farce beneath the overpass returned to me. This was only the second night since that predawn incident.

lines.japanese: 「へえ。なに、戦争終わったの。おまえら、あいつらに勝ったの」
lines.english: “Huh. What, the war's over? You beat them?”

lines.japanese: 俺はさして興味もなさそうに、さりげなく尋ねた。こいつらは（鳳が喋っていないかぎり）俺があのときあの場にいたことを知らないはずだ。
lines.english: I asked casually, doing my best to sound uninterested. Unless Otori had said something, none of them should have known I was there that night.

lines.japanese: 「勝ったつうか……ねえ？」
lines.english: “Beat them? I mean... You know?”

lines.japanese: 森里は仲間たちに微妙な同意を求めた。
lines.english: Morisato looked to his companions for hesitant agreement.

lines.japanese: 「６回表、５対１コールド勝ちっつー感じか？　これから面白くなるとこだったのに、すげえ消化不良で中途半端だよな」
lines.english: “Top of the sixth, five to one, game called. Just when it was getting interesting, too. Hell of an anticlimax—feels unfinished.”

lines.japanese: 「どういうこと」
lines.english: “What happened?”

lines.japanese: 「や・や・や、実はね！　こないだうちの皇帝がね！　Ｒ－ウィングの幹部をひとりフルボッコにしちゃったの、だはは！」
lines.english: “Well, well, well! The other day, our emperor beat one of R-Wing's officers to a pulp! Ahahaha!”

lines.japanese: 「そしたら向こうさん、相当ブルっちゃったみたいでぇ。あっけなく白旗よ、はあ、つまんねえ」
lines.english: “And that must've scared the hell out of them. They waved the white flag just like that. God, how boring.”

lines.japanese: 鳳が倒した幹部──あいつだ、オウム頭の大司教だ。無邪気な戦争ごっこにいきなり本気の飛び道具を持ちだしたりして、仲間にすらドン引かれていた真性のアホだった。
lines.english: The officer Otori had defeated—the parrot-headed Archbishop. A certifiable idiot who had brought a real gun to an innocent little war game and appalled even his own allies.

lines.japanese: ところが柳木原フレイムバーズの鳳翔は、そのアホの凶弾さえ効かない、真性に輪をかけた超真性だった。
lines.english: Yet Kakeru Otori of the Yanagihara Flame Birds was so far beyond certifiable that even that idiot’s bullet had done nothing to him.

lines.japanese: 「いやいやー、強すぎるのも問題っすねえ、かかか」
lines.english: “Yeah, being too strong has its problems. Ka ka ka.”

lines.japanese: 「超真性……」
lines.english: “Certifiable squared...”

lines.japanese: こいつらはＲ－ウィングが恐れをなして降伏したなんて言ってるけど、やつらは恐れをなしたと言うより、敵も味方も頭がおかしいってことに気付いて、まともに相手をするのが馬鹿らしくなったんじゃないだろうか。
lines.english: They said R-Wing had surrendered out of fear. But perhaps they hadn't lost their nerve so much as realized that friend and foe alike were insane, and dealing seriously with either side was a waste of time.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、でも聞いた聞いた～？　そいつ、その、皇帝がボコにしたっつーオンナ男？　なんかねえ、病院から逃げだしちゃったんだって～、ぎゃははケッサク！」
lines.english: “Oh, but did you hear? That guy—the girly man the emperor beat down? Apparently he escaped from the hospital. Gahaha! What a riot!”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　なんだァおい、尿検でもされたらヤバいもん出てくるってかあ？　くくく」
lines.english: “Huh? What's that about? Afraid a piss test would turn up something inconvenient? Heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 「まあでも、もしあのオンナ男が口割っちゃったら、翔さんも面倒なことンなるわけでー。逆にトンズラこいてくれて、ありがたいっちゃーありがたい話なんすよねえ、かかか」
lines.english: “Still, if the girly man talked, it could mean trouble for Kakeru. Looked at that way, I guess we ought to be grateful he skipped out. Ka ka ka.”

lines.japanese: 俺は舌先で口内炎に触れながら会話を聞いていた。
lines.english: I listened while touching the sore inside my mouth with the tip of my tongue.

lines.japanese: 大司教の脱走。それは笑い話で済ませていい問題なのか。そうなると、鳳翔は別の意味で面倒なことになるんじゃないのか。
lines.english: The Archbishop had escaped. Was that really something they could laugh off? Wouldn't that land Kakeru Otori in a different kind of trouble?

lines.japanese: だってそれは、気の触れたストーカーが傷と恨みを募らせたまま野放しになってるってことじゃないか。
lines.english: It meant an unhinged stalker was on the loose, nursing both wounds and a grudge.

lines.japanese: でも、まあ、どっちみち俺には関係が──
lines.english: But either way, it had nothing to do with—

lines.japanese: ──ある、のか？
lines.english: —or did it?

lines.japanese: あのとき俺は、ガード下の輝ききれない明かりの下に、瀕死の大司教を放置した。
lines.english: That night, beneath the lights that could never quite shine under the tracks, I had left the dying archbishop where he lay.

lines.japanese: あのとき俺がそうせず、一般的な義務と倫理に則って警察でも呼んでいれば良かったのか。それとも、くだらないことを考えないよう懇々と語って諭すべきだったのか。
lines.english: Should I have obeyed ordinary duty and ethics and called the police? Or should I have patiently talked him out of his ridiculous ideas?

lines.japanese: ……くそったれだ。巻きこまれただけの俺が、なんでこんな煮えきらない気分にならなきゃなんねえ。
lines.english: ...Goddamn it. I had only been dragged into this. Why the hell did I have to feel so conflicted about it?

lines.japanese: 「隼人君」
lines.english: “Hayato.”

lines.japanese: 暗い思考に没入していった俺を、くいと引きよせる手があった。うだうだ語りあうハゲたちをよそに、香田はさりげない小声で俺だけに言う。
lines.english: A hand gave me a small tug, drawing me out of those dark thoughts. While the bald guys rambled among themselves, Koda spoke in a casual murmur meant for me alone.

lines.japanese: 「ね、いまカズ君たちが話してんのって、たしか佐久間君たちの……」
lines.english: “What Kaz and the others are talking about... That's Sakuma's group, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　あァ、まあ、そうなあ。でも俺らには関係ねー話だから、べつに──」
lines.english: “Huh? Yeah, I guess. But it's got nothing to do with us, so—”

lines.japanese: 「オイオイオイ、なんだよなんだよ！　なんの話だよ、オイラも入れてちょんらいよ！」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, hey! What's this? What're we talking about? Lemme in too! Pretty pleeease!”

lines.japanese: ハゲたちと愉快に話してた森里が、馬鹿みたいにはしゃぎながら俺と香田のあいだに入りこんできた。
lines.english: Morisato abandoned his merry conversation with the bald men and bounced idiotically into the gap between Koda and me.

lines.japanese: 「うんほら、カズ君にも話したじゃん。こないだ私が変なのに絡まれたとき、隼人君が助けてくれたって」
lines.english: “You know, Kaz. I told you. The other day, when that weirdo started harassing me, Hayato saved me.”

lines.japanese: 「え、助けたっけ。ソレ微妙に筋書き違くね？」
lines.english: “Huh? Did I save you? That's not exactly how that scene played out.”

lines.japanese: 「えへへ、隼人君に助けられたの二回目ですね」
lines.english: “Heh heh. That makes twice Hayato has saved me.”

lines.japanese: 「そうだっけ。あと敬語やめろ」
lines.english: “Does it? And knock off the formal act.”

lines.japanese: 一回目。
lines.english: The first time.

lines.japanese: もう半年以上……もっと前か。古い話だからあんま覚えてないんだけど、たしかに言われてみれば、香田となにやらトラブってたバーコードハゲのおっさんを、俺が追いはらったというミニイベントはあった。
lines.english: More than half a year ago... longer, perhaps. I barely remembered anything that old, but now that she mentioned it, there had been a little incident where I chased off a middle-aged man with a barcode comb-over who was having some kind of trouble with Koda.

lines.japanese: 思えば、香田が馴れ馴れしく下の名前で俺を呼ぶようになったのはあれ以来か。
lines.english: Come to think of it, that was when she'd started calling me by my first name as though we'd been friends forever.

lines.japanese: 「さて、隼人君？」
lines.english: “Now then, Hayato?”

lines.japanese: そして香田は今日も馴れ馴れしく下の名前で俺を呼び、こちらを見上げて静かに微笑んでいた。
lines.english: And today again, Koda used my first name with the easy familiarity of an old friend and smiled quietly up at me.

lines.japanese: 「あなた、もう団地妻とは別れたですか？」
lines.english: “Have you broken up with the apartment wife yet?”

lines.japanese: ……なんの話だ。
lines.english: ...What the hell was she talking about?

lines.japanese: 「なんの話だ？」
lines.english: “What the hell is she talking about?”

lines.japanese: 森里が俺のはてなを代弁してくれた。
lines.english: Morisato gave voice to the question mark floating above my head.

lines.japanese: 「も、聞いてよカズ君。なんか最近ー、隼人君の身辺にママチャリ女がうろついてる疑惑浮上ー」
lines.english: “Listen to this, Kaz. New evidence suggests some mom-bike woman has been lurking around Hayato lately.”

lines.japanese: 「ハァ？　マジかよ成田、おまえ節操ねえなあ。鳴さんの次は人妻かよ」
lines.english: “What? Seriously, Narita? No restraint at all. First Naru, now a married woman?”

lines.japanese: 「なに、誰っ！　マルさん！？　誰マルさんって、誰誰！」
lines.english: “What? Who? Maru? Who's Maru? Who, who?”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、だから違げっつってんだろ。マルさんもママさんも、ぜんぶ空想上の人物じゃねーか。知らねーよ、知るかよそんなやつら」
lines.english: “Shut up. I told you, that's not it. Maru and Mommy are both figments of your imagination. I don't know them. How the hell should I know people like that?”

lines.japanese: 「だーって隼人君、この前、子持ち女の自転車探してあげてるって言ってたじゃーん」
lines.english: “But Hayato, the other day you said you were looking for a bike belonging to a woman with a kid.”

lines.japanese: 「だから。なんでおまえは話がいちいち微妙に変わんだよ。なんだ子持ち女って。どっから出てきたんだ、そのガキは。キャベツ畑か。想像妊娠か」
lines.english: “I keep telling you. Why do you change the story a little every single time? What do you mean, ‘a woman with a kid’? Where'd this kid come from? A cabbage patch? Phantom pregnancy?”

lines.japanese: 俺はそこで森里に視点を移した。
lines.english: At that point, I shifted my gaze to Morisato.

lines.japanese: 「いや、違くてな？　そうじゃなくて、ほら俺、便利屋みてえな副業してんじゃん」
lines.english: “No, listen. It wasn't like that. You know I run that little handyman operation on the side?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。ピンクのクレープ屋で受付してンだろ」
lines.english: “Yeah. You take requests at the pink crêpe stand.”

lines.japanese: 「おう、そんでこのまえ、鳳の妹が俺んとこ来て。なんか、盗まれたチャリを探してほしいとか言って」
lines.english: “Right. And the other day, Kakeru's little sister came by. Wanted me to find a stolen bike.”

lines.japanese: 「へえ、鳴さん本当に行ったんだ」
lines.english: “Huh. So Naru really did go to you.”
“...What?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だって、あの子に成田工務店のこと教えたの──ねえＬＲさん、俺らだもんねえ？」
lines.english: “Well, we're the ones who told her about Narita Construction. Right, LR?”

lines.japanese: 「おお、そうよ」
lines.english: “Sure are.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、翔さんに言われてだけどさ」
lines.english: “Well, Kakeru told us to.”

lines.japanese: 「馬鹿おまッ、それ内緒だろ！」
lines.english: “Idiot! That was supposed to be a secret!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、やべ、そうだった！」
lines.english: “Oh, shit! Right!”
“...Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: 考えてみればそうだ。俺は情報誌に広告を出したり街角でビラを配ってるわけじゃない。俺のところへ来る客はみんな、辿ってみれば俺の知ってる誰かから紹介を受けているはずなんだ。
lines.english: When I thought about it, that made sense. I didn't advertise in magazines or hand out flyers on street corners. Trace the connection far enough and every client who found me must have been referred by someone I knew.

lines.japanese: しかし内緒らしいので、俺はそのことを忘れるよう努めた。まったく、どいつもこいつも面倒くせえ。
lines.english: But apparently it was a secret, so I did my best to forget it. Every last one of them was a pain in the ass.

lines.japanese: 「へー。翔さんって子持ちの妹がいたんだ？」
lines.english: “Huh. So Kakeru has a little sister with a kid?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、おまえも」
lines.english: “You too—”

lines.japanese: 俺は香田の喉首に、親指と人差し指を引っかけた。
lines.english: I hooked my thumb and forefinger around Koda's throat.

lines.japanese: 「いいかげん、子持ちから、離れろっ」
lines.english: “—let—go—of ‘with a kid’ already!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あー、ああー！」
lines.english: “Aah, aah, aaah!”

lines.japanese: 鳴にやるみたいに、香田の体を前後に揺すぶった。笑いながら大袈裟にわめく女。森里の冷めた目。俺は手を離した。
lines.english: I rocked Koda back and forth the way I did Naru. She shrieked theatrically through her laughter. Morisato watched with cold eyes. I let go.

lines.japanese: 「ったく……森里。こいつ、伝言ゲームで確実にグループを負けへ導くタイプだろ」
lines.english: “Honestly... Morisato, she'd lose any team a game of Telephone, wouldn't she?”

lines.japanese: 「チャリってソレ、どんなの？　名前とか書いてあんの？」
lines.english: “This bike—what's it like? Does it have a name written on it?”

lines.japanese: やつは俺の質問を無視して、べつの質問で返してきた。失礼なやつだ。
lines.english: He ignored my question and answered with another. Rude bastard.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ……なんか赤くて背もたれ付いてるらしいけど」
lines.english: “Yeah, well... apparently it's red and has a backrest.”

lines.japanese: 「背もたれ？　へえ、珍しい。そんならわりと探しやすいかもな」
lines.english: “A backrest? Huh. Unusual. Might make it pretty easy to find.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、俺も最初はそう思ったんだけど、なかなかどうしてこれが。どうにもこうにも」
lines.english: “That's what I thought at first, but no such luck. No way, no how.”

lines.japanese: 「ニッチモ・サッチーモ？」
lines.english: “No-Way McNo-How?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、そんな感じ」
lines.english: “Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「だめだめじゃーん。隼人君そんなめんどい仕事、引きうけんなしー」
lines.english: “Then you're hopeless. Hayato, don't take stupid jobs like that.”

lines.japanese: 「あァ？　いや、べつに引きうけてはいねーよ。仕事としては断ったけど、なんとなく手伝える範囲で探してやってるだけだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? I didn't take it. I turned it down as a job. I'm just sort of helping her look where I can.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？　なんで？」
lines.english: “What? Why?”

lines.japanese: 「はぁ？　いや、なんでっておまえ、べつにそんなん理由はいらねーだろ。困ってるひとがいたら、なんとなく助けるだろフツー」
lines.english: “Huh? What do you mean, why? You don't need a reason. Someone's in trouble, you sort of help. That's normal.”

lines.japanese: 「うん。普通はそうだけど、隼人君、いままで普通じゃなかったじゃん」
lines.english: “Sure, normally. But you've never been normal before.”

lines.japanese: 「ばかおまえ、普通だっつうの。どの角度から見たって普通の善人だっつうの。んだてめ、失礼なことぬかしてっと善人だてらにブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Idiot, of course I'm normal. From any angle you like, I'm an ordinary good Samaritan. Keep insulting me. I'll fucking kill you, asshole—good Samaritan or not.”

lines.japanese: 「うーっそ！　ないない、そんなマジありえないって！　だって、うちらとかハイパー困ってても『俺には関係ねーけど』とかゆって超スルーすんのが隼人君じゃん！」
lines.english: “Liar! No, no, literally impossible! We can be in the worst trouble ever and you'll go, ‘Nothing to do with me,’ and cruise right past. That's who Hayato is!”

lines.japanese: 「それはまァ、ほらアレだよ、あの、こう見えてちょっぴり照れ屋さんなところがあるからさ俺は」
lines.english: “Well, you see, that's... I may not look it, but I happen to be a teensy bit shy.”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅぅ～ん……」
lines.english: “Riiight...”

lines.japanese: 香田は疑いに満ちた眼差しで俺を眺めてから、森里の方へ振りむいた。
lines.english: Koda studied me with eyes full of suspicion, then turned to Morisato.

lines.japanese: 「カズ君、その妹さんって可愛いの？」
lines.english: “Kaz, is this little sister cute?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そらまぁ“鳳凰寺カケル”と同じ血が流れてるわけだし、それなりには」
lines.english: “Well, she has the same blood as ‘Kakeru Hououji,’ so she's decent-looking.”

lines.japanese: 「……イケメン絵描きの妹か」
lines.english: “...The handsome illustrator's sister.”

lines.japanese: そういえばこいつらから聞いたことがあった。鳳翔は不良の頭領のくせして裏じゃ──訂正、表じゃ──イラストーターなんて冗談みたいなバイトをしてるらしい。こっちの顔がバレたらソッコーお払い箱だろうに。
lines.english: Come to think of it, they'd told me. Despite leading a band of delinquents, Kakeru Otori secretly—correction, publicly—held the absurd side job of illustrator under the name Kakeru Hououji. If that crowd ever connected this face to the name, he'd be out of a job on the spot.

lines.japanese: 「え？　てことは？　その妹も背が高くて？　足が長くて？　とにかく細くて超美人？」
lines.english: “Wait, then is she tall? Long legs? Super skinny and amazingly beautiful?”

lines.japanese: 「ぷっ」
lines.english: “Pfft.”

lines.japanese: 思わず吹きだしてしまった。いったい誰の話をしてるんだ、こいつは。
lines.english: A laugh escaped me. Who in the world was she describing?

lines.japanese: 「ちくしょー顔かよ……」
lines.english: “Damn it. So it *is* the face...”

lines.japanese: しかし香田はなにやら誤解してる予感。
lines.english: Koda, however, seemed to have misunderstood.

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、でも……でも、わりとアレだぜ、あの、好み分かれる系？」
lines.english: “Y-yeah, but... you know. She’s kind of polarizing?”

lines.japanese: 「俺なんか、まあその、どっちかっちゅーと……や、どっちかっちゅーとだけど？　ま、あえて？　あえてどっちかっつーなら？　つーならまあ、俺は亜」
lines.english: “I mean, personally, I guess I'd... No, only if I had to choose, okay? If I absolutely *had* to? Then I'd probably choose A—”

lines.japanese: 「相手にとって不足なーし！」
lines.english: “A worthy rival!”

lines.japanese: 香田はなぜか俺に指を一本突きつけていた。俺は眉間に皺を寄せてその指を見つめながら──
lines.english: For some reason, Koda leveled one finger at me. I stared at it, a deep crease between my brows, and—

lines.japanese: ──ゆっくり首を横にひねった。さっぱりのボディランゲージ。
lines.english: —slowly tilted my head. The universal sign for *no idea.*

lines.japanese: 「なんだあ？　森里、なんでこいついきなり、会ったこともない鳳・妹に張りあってんの」
lines.english: “What? Morisato, why is she suddenly competing with Kakeru's sister when they've never met?”

lines.japanese: 「知らねえよ！」
lines.english: “How should I know!”

lines.japanese: 怒られてしまった。こいつはこいつで、なに急に不機嫌になってんだ。
lines.english: He snapped at me. And what had suddenly put *him* in a mood?

lines.japanese: 「ＬＲさーん、なー、俺らも鳴さんのチャリ探してみるー？」
lines.english: “Hey, LR. Think we should help look for Naru's bike?”

lines.japanese: やつは俺をシカトして、後ろのでかいハゲたちに声をかけた。
lines.english: Ignoring me, he called to the large bald men behind us.

lines.japanese: 「おおっ？　あー、おう、いんじゃねーソレ」
lines.english: “Oh? Ah, sure. Why not?”

lines.japanese: 「見つけてあげたら、翔さんも喜ぶかもしんないっすよね？」
lines.english: “If we find it, Kakeru might be happy too, right?”

lines.japanese: 「あのひと自分じゃバレてないつもりだけど、実際むっつりシスコンだもんねぇ」
lines.english: “He thinks nobody's noticed, but he's secretly obsessed with his sister.”

lines.japanese: なにやら連中はそこそこ乗り気な雰囲気。
lines.english: The group seemed fairly keen on the idea.

lines.japanese: さらに「盗んだやつ見つけたらフクロにしようぜ」という提案が挙がってから、やつらは俄然盛りあがりだした。
lines.english: Then someone suggested they beat the thief senseless if they found him. At that, their enthusiasm burst into flame.

lines.japanese: やべ、俺なんか余計なこと喋っちゃったかもしんねえ……。
lines.english: Shit. Maybe I'd said more than I should have...

lines.japanese: 「まー、どーせ、新しい敵役が見つかるまでＹＦＢも暇だしねえ」
lines.english: “YFB's got nothing to do until we find a new villain anyway.”

lines.japanese: 「カズ君、暇暇って言うけど、明日から期末テスト始まるんでしょ？」
lines.english: “Kaz, you keep saying you're bored, but don't final exams start tomorrow?”

lines.japanese: 「うん。だからガッコ早く終わんじゃん」
lines.english: “Yeah. Means school gets out early.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、勉強しろよ」
lines.english: “No. It means you should study.”

lines.japanese: 「はッ！　いんだよ、も、そーゆーのは。卒業さえできりゃ、も、どーでもさ」
lines.english: “Hah! I'm done with all that. As long as I graduate, who even cares?”

lines.japanese: 森里は強気に笑いとばそうとしたみたいだけど、どうにも力が抜けてて、なんだかいじけて自棄になってるみたいだった。
lines.english: Morisato tried to laugh it off boldly, but there was no strength in it. He looked sulky, almost desperate.

lines.japanese: 「Ｕｈ、卒業はいいけどよ、ペガおまえ、まだ進路決まってねンだろ？」
lines.english: “Uh, graduation's fine, but Pega, you still haven't decided what comes after, have you?”

lines.japanese: ペガはペガサスのペガ。チーム内における森里和馬の通り名だ。ちょっと痛々しいと思うだろうが、そこはドラキュラのドラに免じて許してやってほしい。
lines.english: Pega was short for Pegasus, Morisato Kazuma’s name inside the team. A little embarrassing, you say? On behalf of Dra, short for Dracula, I ask that you let it slide.

lines.japanese: 「いやあ、決まってますって。プーすよ、プー。あとはもう、どこでバイトすっかぐれーで」
lines.english: “Sure I have. I'm gonna be a bum. All that's left is deciding where to work part-time.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、もーナンダソレ、勿体なくなーい？　三年前、せっかくあんなベンキョしていいガッコ入ったのに。おばさんたち、超かわいそザウルスじゃん」
lines.english: “What? That's such a waste! Three years ago you studied super hard to get into a good school. Your parents must be, like, total pity-sauruses.”

lines.japanese: 「言うなよ、そうゆうさあ。本人がいちばん気にしてんだからさあ」
lines.english: “Don't say that. I'm the one it bothers most.”

lines.japanese: 「つうかぁー、チャケバあんとき頑張りすぎちゃったのが間違いだったんだよねぇ。中途半端なアタマで背伸びした酬いがこれだもん。あーもーやだやだ、勉強なんかしたくねーっつうの」
lines.english: “Honestly, busting my ass back then was the mistake. This is what I get for trying to punch above my weight with a second-rate brain. God, I'm sick of it. I don't wanna study anymore.”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　なに和馬、おまえ進学校のくせに進学しねーの」
lines.english: “Huh? Kazuma, you go to a college-prep school and you're not going to college?”

lines.japanese: 「だから聞くなって。嫌味かよ。出来るわきゃねーだろ、なんも準備してねーのに」
lines.english: “I told you not to ask. Rubbing it in? How could I get in? I haven’t prepared for anything.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、いまからすりゃいいじゃん」
lines.english: “Then start now.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうじゃん。ソレいい考え、成田ちゃん今日も冴えてるね～」
lines.english: “Hey, he's right. Great idea. Narita, you're sharp today.”

lines.japanese: 「だろ」
lines.english: “Damn right.”

lines.japanese: 「アホか、いまさら間に合うかっつーの」
lines.english: “Idiot. It's way too late.”

lines.japanese: 「願書の提出？　まだギリ間に合うんじゃない？」
lines.english: “The application deadlines? You could probably still squeak in, couldn't you?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃねーよ、受験ベンキョーだよ。いまから二、三ヵ月必死ンなったとこで、何がどーなるっつんだよ」
lines.english: “Not that. Studying for the exams. What's killing myself for two or three months gonna change?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ、どーにかなるかもしんねーじゃん」
lines.english: “Who knows? Might change something.”

lines.japanese: 「ハア～ア？」
lines.english: “Whaaat?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ、そうだよねえ。だってカズ君、基礎は一度叩きこんでるわけじゃん。でいて、あと三ヵ月ちょー猛勉強とかしたら、意外とどっかヌルッと滑りこめちゃうかも」
lines.english: “That's true. You had the fundamentals drilled into you once, Kaz. Study like crazy for the next three months and you might just slip into someplace or other.”

lines.japanese: 「Ｒｉｇｈｔ！　馬鹿みてぇに高望みさえしなけりゃあ、ありえない話でもねえだろ」
lines.english: “Right! As long as you don't aim stupidly high, it's hardly impossible.”

lines.japanese: 「あとほら、二部狙いにしてハードル下げるとかって手も」
lines.english: “You could lower the bar and aim for a university's night program.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ、おいィィ……ちょっとみんな、それマジで言ってんのぉ？」
lines.english: “Wait, heeey... Are you people actually serious?”

lines.japanese: 「マジっつうか、べつにマジじゃなくたっていいじゃん。とりあえずネタ的に受けて、受かりゃ儲けもんじゃん」
lines.english: “Serious or not, who cares? Just take it for kicks. If you get in, that’s a bonus.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ほーんと。きょう成田ちゃん冴えまくり～、いったい何キメてんの～？」
lines.english: “Oh, he's right. Narita, you're on fire today. What're you on?”

lines.japanese: 「キメてねえよ。な香田、そういうの記念受験っつうんだっけ？」
lines.english: “Nothing. Hey, Koda, what's it called? Taking the exam just to say you did?”

lines.japanese: 「ちょーっと隼人君、失礼過ぎだしー、カズ君ほんとは頭いいんだからねー」
lines.english: “Hayato, that is *way* too rude! Kaz is actually smart, you know!”

lines.japanese: 「痛って！」
lines.english: “Ow!”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ……てめ、なんだよその手。爪切れ爪」
lines.english: “Hey... what the hell is with your hands? Cut your nails.”

lines.japanese: 「えぇー？　これダメぇー？」
lines.english: “What? These are no good?”

lines.japanese: 香田は十本の指を広げて街灯にかざしながら、幼稚園児のお遊戯みたいに表、裏、表、裏と何度もひるがえした。十枚の小さなキャンバスに描かれた、ラメ入りの雪景色がひらひらと揺れる。
lines.english: Koda spread all ten fingers beneath the streetlight and turned them front, back, front, back, again and again like a kindergarten dance. Glittering snowscapes painted on ten tiny canvases fluttered in the light.

lines.japanese: 「うそぉーん……かあいいネイルだと思うんだけどなあ……」
lines.english: “No waaay... I thought my nails were cute...”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ、かあいいネイルだろー。コーダインに謝れよなー、隼人先パぁイ」
lines.english: “They *are* cute. Apologize to Kodine, Hayato, maaan.”

lines.japanese: 「あ……いや、まあ、絵がどうとかじゃなくてな。要はこう、人様を引っかかないよう気を付けろっつー話よ。な、ほら、生爪とかペリッて剥がれちゃうと意外と痛いだろ」
lines.english: “Ah... no, I didn't mean the art. I meant be careful not to scratch people. You know, it hurts more than you'd think when a whole nail peels off.”

lines.japanese: やつがしょんぼりしかけたので、俺は適当なフォローを入れた。しょんぼりされちゃ仕方ない。俺はこう見えて、しょんぼりには弱いんだ。
lines.english: She had begun to wilt, so I offered whatever reassurance came to hand. Couldn't help it. Despite appearances, I was weak against wilting.

lines.japanese: 「ん？　どしたのペガ。なんかキメたいの？」
lines.english: “Hm? What's up, Pega? Feel like getting high?”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　ああいや……へへ」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh, no... heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、あっぶねーの。いま一瞬、さわやかキャンパスライフとか脳裏かすめちゃったよ俺。かかか、バカじゃねーの俺。ぎゃははは」
lines.english: “Nothing. For a second there, I almost let myself picture some wholesome campus life. Ha ha. What an idiot. Ha ha ha.”

lines.japanese: 森里はべつに誰も笑ってないのに、ひとりでバカウケしていた。
lines.english: Nobody else was laughing, but Morisato found himself hilarious.

lines.japanese: それから両腕をＷの字に広げて、嘘くさいあくびをかました。
lines.english: Then he spread his arms into a W and delivered an obviously fake yawn.

lines.japanese: 「かはぁ～あ……しっかし暇だなあ。ねー、これからどーするー？　ダーツでも行くー？」
lines.english: “Haaaaah... God, I'm bored. Hey, what now? Wanna go play darts?”

lines.japanese: 「ダーツ！？　おっけ、よーし　行くぞこらー！」
lines.english: “Darts!? Okay! Let’s go, dammit!”

lines.japanese: 森里の提案に賛同の声がいくつか続いた。香田なんか、子供みたいに握りこぶしをぐっと天に掲げていた。
lines.english: Several voices seconded Morisato's proposal. Koda even thrust a little clenched fist into the sky like a child.

lines.japanese: 俺は個室ビデオの壁にもたれてそれを見ながら、ケツの下で右手を閉じたり開いたりした。
lines.english: Still leaning against the video-shop wall, I watched them and opened and closed my right hand down by my side, out of sight.

lines.japanese: 「ねー、隼人君もたまにはいっしょに行こーよ！」
lines.english: “Hey, Hayato, come with us for once!”
“Ah—”

lines.japanese: 喉が絡んで、俺はひとつ咳払いをした。
lines.english: My throat caught. I cleared it once.

lines.japanese: 「──あぁ、まぁ、また今度な」
lines.english: “—Yeah, well. Maybe next time.”

lines.japanese: 「えー、もお隼人君いっつもそーじゃーん」
lines.english: “What? Hayato, you *always* say that.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかあ？　いつもとはちょっと違うんじゃねーの」
lines.english: “Does he? Sounded a little different from usual to me.”

lines.japanese: 「ええ？」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 「『また今度』だって。そんな前向きな回答、初めて聞いた気がするんですけどねえ成田さん」
lines.english: “He said, ‘Maybe next time.’ Don't think I've ever heard such a positive answer from you before, Mr. Narita.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　そうか？」
lines.english: “Huh? Really?”

lines.japanese: 気のせいだろ、と言って俺は連中と別れた。
lines.english: I told them they were imagining it and went my separate way.

lines.japanese: ピンフ通りの浮かれた人の波を掻きわけながら、俺は試しに、香田の真似をして右手で作ったグーを頭上に突きあげてみた。
lines.english: As I pushed through the festive tide on Pinfu Street, I tried imitating Koda. I made a fist with my right hand and thrust it above my head.

lines.japanese: それは思ったよりも簡単な動作だった。
lines.english: It was an easier movement than I had expected.
